sections.heading: Why Are Inno Amino Products Labeled “Not for Human Consumption?"
sections.html:
Research peptides are labeled “not for human consumption” for regulatory and economic reasons — not because they are approved for medical use or intended to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any disease.

Rather than exhaustively detailing regulatory frameworks, the following highlights the primary factors behind this designation:

F.D.A. Approval Costs

Obtaining F.D.A. approval for pharmaceutical use requires substantial financial investment, often reaching millions of dollars, placing it beyond the scope of most independent research laboratories and peptide suppliers.

Scope of Required Clinical Trials

Formal approval mandates extensive preclinical and clinical trials conducted under strict regulatory protocols. These large-scale studies require significant capital and infrastructure, which are typically accessible only to major pharmaceutical manufacturers.

Patent and Commercial Limitations

Many peptides consist of amino acid sequences naturally occurring in the human body and therefore do not qualify for meaningful patent protection. This limits commercial incentives to pursue costly regulatory approval pathways.

Market and Prescribing Dynamics

Even when pharmaceutical alternatives exist, approved medications may be prescribed off-label, further reducing incentives to pursue separate approval for comparable peptide compounds.

Quality and Research Standards

While not approved for human consumption, many peptides are widely referenced in scientific and academic research. Reputable suppliers focus on maintaining consistent research-grade standards, including third-party analytical testing to verify compound identity and purity prior to distribution.

All products offered by Inno Amino are sold strictly for research purposes only and are not intended for human or veterinary use.

Inno Amino products are sold strictly for Research Use Only (RUO) and are available exclusively to qualified researchers working in controlled laboratory environments. These materials are not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for human or veterinary use, including clinical applications, therapeutic purposes, or any form of consumption.

Inno Amino operates in alignment with regulatory standards, including Section 503A of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA), and restricts product availability to professional research use only.

Important Notice: Inno Amino does not offer guidance, advice, or recommendations on product use or experimental applications. Researchers are solely responsible for consulting appropriate experts to establish and follow proper research protocols.
